title: When a drug is misbranded under 21 U.S.C. 352
rule_summary: Under 21 U.S.C. 352 a drug is deemed misbranded, among other grounds: (a)(1) if its labeling is false or misleading in any particular; (b) if in package form unless it bears a label containing the name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor and an accurate statement of the quantity of the contents; (f) unless its labeling bears adequate directions for use and adequate warnings; (g) if it purports to be a drug recognized in an official compendium, unless packaged and labeled as the compendium prescribes; (h) if the Secretary has found it to be a drug liable to deterioration, unless packaged and labeled as the Secretary's regulations require; (i) if its container is so made, formed, or filled as to be misleading, if it is an imitation of another drug, or if it is offered for sale under the name of another drug; (j) if it is dangerous to health when used in the dosage or manner, or with the frequency or duration, prescribed, recommended, or suggested in its labeling; and (p) if its packaging or labeling is in violation of an applicable regulation issued under 15 U.S.C. 1472 or 1473. Paragraphs (k) and (l) of section 352 are repealed.
exam_relevance: Tests the misbranding grounds that turn on labeling and packaging, which are the grounds a dispensed prescription is largely exempted from under 21 U.S.C. 353(b)(2).

authority.name: Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act

common_confusions: Misbranding concerns labeling and packaging; defects in the drug's strength, quality or purity are adulteration.
verification_notes: Read on 2026-09-17 in 21 U.S.C. 352 on the Office of the Law Revision Counsel's United States Code site.
